title: F1 announces 2027 calendar: 24 races, 10 sprints, Portugal and Turkey return
dek: Formula 1 announced its 2027 calendar on September 16 with 24 races and 10 sprint events, up from six this season. Portugal returns to the schedule for the first time since 2021, and Turkey makes its comeback after a five-year absence. Monaco will host a sprint race for the first time.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Sprint races will double from six to 10 in 2027, representing F1's expansion of a format the sport says has proven successful with fans.
bottom_line: F1 announces 2027 calendar: 24-race schedule with sprint races doubled to 10 events; Portugal and Turkey return after absences.
body: Formula 1 released its 2027 season schedule on September 16, cementing sprint racing as a core format while restoring Portugal and Turkey to a calendar that will expand to 10 sprint events, double the current six.

The 24-race campaign opens in Bahrain on March 14 and closes in Abu Dhabi on December 12, per the Guardian's reporting. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said the schedule reflects the sport's growth, stating: "Formula One continues to go from strength-to-strength, attracting new audiences around the globe. Week after week, the world's greatest drivers will battle on some of the most challenging tracks in motor sport, supported by F1's outstanding teams, world-class manufacturers, and global partners."

The sprint expansion lands Monaco in the sprint format for the first time. Five venues will host sprints for the first time: Bahrain, Australia, Japan, Monaco, and Abu Dhabi. Five others will see the format return: Montreal, Silverstone, Monza, São Paulo, and Lusail. F1 considers the sprint events successful and popular with fans, according to the Guardian's coverage.

Portugal returns with its meeting in Portimão on June 20, its first appearance since 2021 when it served as a Covid-era replacement. Turkey's comeback is scheduled for October 3 after hosting during the pandemic in 2021 but not in regular competition since 2011. The Turkish GP remains subject to FIA circuit homologation, a technical approval process that introduces uncertainty around the event's final confirmation.

Barcelona does not appear on the 2027 calendar; it will now rotate hosting with the Belgian GP at Spa on alternate years. The Dutch GP at Zandvoort held its final race in 2026. All four Middle East races are scheduled in their normal slots, though F1 has contingency plans if geopolitical disruptions require cancellations, with Imola expected to host the season finale in December if needed. The calendar includes three triple-headers: Australia, Japan and China in April; Azerbaijan, Turkey and Singapore in September-October; and the United States, Mexico and Brazil in October-November.

Las Vegas will not run back-to-back with Qatar and Abu Dhabi for the first time since the race joined the schedule, with a one-week gap after Nevada. The Silverstone round takes place July 2-4. Pre-season testing is scheduled for February 24-27 in Sakhir, Bahrain.

The Bottom Line: The Turkish GP's FIA homologation requirement and F1's stated contingency plans for Middle East races signal that geopolitical risk persists despite the sport's commitment to the 2027 schedule as stated. The sprint doubling and return of Portugal and Turkey will be confirmed or complicated between now and the season's opening in March 2027.
